ENGLISH — TERMLY EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. goes

2. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes: Compound Nouns.

3. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

4. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

5. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the Library

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language: Telephone Etiquette.

7. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

8. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only a joining word

9. When practising Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)

   A. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.

   C. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

11. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, which approach is best? (1 mark)

12. When practising Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

   A. run
   B. happiness
   C. quickly
   D. blue

14. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)

15. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. Only one word repeated
   C. No full stops
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Narrative Composition 14.5.1 Descriptive writing 15.5.1 Functional Writing – not and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 13.5.1 Creative Narrative Composition: Idioms and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 14.1.1 Pronunciation and Intonation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Intonation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
